title: session-morning.sh step [3] --window under-fetches after a MISSED morning (multi-session gap)
notes: Step [3] now passes --window $session_date..$session_date, correct for the designed one-session-per-morning cadence. But window.from is the START of the KRX witness fetch (fetch_state.rs seeds krx_cursor from window.from, runs to krx_through), so if a morning is MISSED the gap spans 2+ sessions and only the latest day gets a witness — intermediate days stay Unknown while the bounded ingest tries to advance across them. Invisible on 2026-07-31 because the gap was exactly one day (frontier 20260729 -> session 20260730). Fix direction: derive window.from from the daily watermark in the ingest checkpoint (the script already reads it for count_advanced/SYMS) instead of the session date. Verify the ingest's behavior on an Unknown intermediate day before choosing the bound.

title: session-morning.sh step [7] pace check KILLS the ingest on a catch-up run, leaving a PARTIAL catalog
notes: The in-ingest pace check polls every 30s and kills ls-ingest as soon as it projects past LS_SM_INGEST_BY (default 09:05), then exits 40. That is right for the attended path it was built for — a universe landing after 09:10 is useless because head v34 builds its opening range only from 09:00-15:00 live bars. It is WRONG for a catch-up run, where the mount is already conceded and the whole point is to advance the catalog: the kill leaves a partial watermark distribution, i.e. exactly the half-finished state the catch-up exists to prevent. Nothing in the script distinguishes the two callers. Workaround used on 2026-07-31: LS_SM_INGEST_BY=09:40 with LS_SM_UNIVERSE_BY left at 09:10, so the ingest completes and the clean stand-down happens at the step [8] gate instead. Fix direction: an explicit catch-up mode (or --no-pace-gate) that skips the step [7] kill while keeping the step [8] universe refusal.
